s1.syndrome_frame: Worsening skin condition with systemic symptoms in a patient with a history of autoimmune disorders
salient_findings: Diffuse ill-defined erythema and mild edema of the face and eyelids
Violaceous to erythematous patches on the joints, periungual skin, and chest
Scaly erythematous plaques on lateral leg
key_facts: Patient has a history of biopsy-proven psoriasis
Patient has a history of juvenile dermatomyositis (DM)
Juvenile DM had been in remission for several years
Patient previously treated with adalimumab, etanercept, methotrexate, guselkumab, ustekinumab, and topical corticosteroids
Patient experienced fatigue, difficulty picking up her child, and climbing stairs after starting new medication
Physical examination revealed diffuse ill-defined erythema and mild edema of the face and eyelids
Laboratory evaluation results were negative or normal, including creatine kinase levels and aldolase levels

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of biopsy-proven juvenile dermatomyositis and is experiencing worsening skin condition with systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of biopsy-proven psoriasis and is experiencing worsening skin condition

shortlist.label: Lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is experiencing systemic symptoms and skin manifestations that could be consistent with lupus

shortlist.label: Amyopathic dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of dermatomyositis and is experiencing skin manifestations without significant muscle involvement

shortlist.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of autoimmune disorders and is experiencing overlapping symptoms of different conditions

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of juvenile dermatomyositis and is presenting with skin manifestations such as diffuse ill-defined erythema, violaceous to erythematous patches, and scaly erythematous plaques, but laboratory evaluation results including creatine kinase levels and aldolase levels are normal, indicating no active muscle disease, which is consistent with amyopathic dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: Normal creatine kinase and aldolase levels suggest no active muscle disease.

rejected.label: Psoriasis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of psoriasis, the current presentation includes features not typical of psoriasis, such as violaceous patches and photodistributed poikiloderma.

rejected.label: Lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: The presentation lacks typical features of lupus, such as malar rash, oral ulcers, or specific laboratory findings.

rejected.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
rejected.why: The clinical presentation does not include a combination of features typical of different autoimmune diseases, such as lupus, scleroderma, and rheumatoid arthritis, which would be expected in mixed connective tissue disease.
